summary.headline: Arvaya Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% QoQ to ₹40 crore, but occupancy fell to 38% as newly acquired beds ramp up.
summary.overview: Arvaya Healthcare held its first earnings call covering Q2 and H1 FY27, the first full half with the Secure Hospitals acquisition consolidated. Q2 revenue was about ₹40 crore (up 35% QoQ), EBITDA ₹5.24 crore at a 13% margin, and PAT ₹1.37 crore versus ₹0.53 crore in Q1. Operating beds rose to 517 from 262 a year earlier, and occupancy fell to 38% from 48% because newer hospitals run at about 27%. Management reiterated 791 beds operational by December 2026, a 1,200-bed FY28 target, and a ₹206 crore rights issue to fund equipment and fit-outs.

segments.name: Established hospitals
segments.commentary: Mature hospitals ran at about 46% average occupancy (management cited a 48-56% range); the flagship Mysore unit has 125 beds and ran at 56.5% in H1.

segments.name: Newer acquired hospitals
segments.commentary: Occupancy rose to about 27% from 10-11% earlier; the Mysore II hospital added in August has the highest revenue per occupied bed at ₹31,000.

segments.name: Government schemes (PMJAY, Yashaswini)
segments.commentary: Government-scheme patients are 15-20% of mix; management said they help utilisation but carry lower realisation than private and insurance patients.

guidance_outlook: 791 beds to be fully operational by December 2026 (517 operating today), with fit-outs and medical equipment under way.
220 beds signed via MOUs in Jalna, Kandiyan and Shimoga, due by end of next financial year (FY28).
Target of about 1,200 beds in FY28 and about 2,400 beds by FY30 through operating partnerships and acquisitions.
Revenue trajectory targeted at over ₹600 crore by FY30; EBITDA margin to be held at current levels, with management expecting 13-14% going forward.
Arvaya app to launch within the financial year; all Secure patients to be enabled on the app by next quarter; annual technology spend to stay within about ₹2-3 crore.
Goa resort to be repurposed; management expects 15-20% margins once operating, with numbers to be shared by end of next quarter.
capex_capacity: Hospital network: nine multi-speciality hospitals across seven cities in Karnataka and Maharashtra, 517 operating beds, 222+ specialities; all units leased except one in Goa; capital goes to medical equipment and technology.
Investment per bed about ₹24 lakh; a new 100-bed hospital costs about ₹20-25 crore (management cited ₹23.6 crore), with management targeting 5-10% annual return on capital at maturity.
Rights issue of about ₹206 crore planned to fund medical equipment, fit-outs and acquisitions.
Swasthya Institute of Gastroenterology (Shimoga) integrated from 1 November through a 100% share-swap deal with no cash payout; it runs about ₹1 crore monthly revenue at 15-18% profit margin.
Diagnostics: plans for a large laboratory and satellite labs and home collection; no timeline given beyond next quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 OPD visits rose 5-10% and discharges more than 20% QoQ; occupancy is said to be rising quarter on quarter as new beds are fitted out.

Revenue per occupied bed rose about 17% per the call, driven mainly by surgery and specialty mix in cardiology, neurosciences, nephrology and robotic surgery; tariff increases were described as nominal.
Expansion strategy is regional density in Karnataka and Maharashtra border districts (Kolhapur, Solapur belt) before moving to other states.

qa_highlights.question: Why has occupancy fallen to about 30% from 48% a year ago, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to newly acquired hospitals running at about 27% occupancy against 48-56% at mature hospitals. OPDs rose 5-10% and discharges more than 20% QoQ, and occupancy is expected to normalise as fit-outs finish.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in revenue per bed?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly surgery and specialty mix, with only nominal price increases. All nine hospitals are largely super-specialty.

qa_highlights.question: How large is government-scheme exposure and how does it affect profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Government schemes are 15-20% of patients. They have lower realisation but raise occupancy, and management said the EBITDA impact is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a liquidity constraint given borrowings of ₹31 crore against cash of ₹3 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings funded medical equipment and fit-outs for the acquired beds. Management expects operating cash flow to rise next year.

qa_highlights.question: How are patient data protection, cybersecurity and DPDP compliance handled?
qa_highlights.answer: The stack was built to HL7 FHIR standards with DPDP compliance designed in, and consent will be taken before data use. The clinical intelligence engine is hospital-agnostic and still in pilot.

qa_highlights.question: What are the diagnostics and app monetisation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab and radiology network plans are in progress, with more detail promised next quarter. The app will be free for engagement at first, with monetisation still under deliberation; about 30,000 patient records have been ingested.

risks_watch: Occupancy at 38% versus 48% a year ago; recovery depends on 791-bed fit-out and ramp-up of newer hospitals reaching around 50%.
Execution of the ₹206 crore rights issue and the funding need for 1,200 beds by FY28 and 2,400 by FY30.
Net debt of about ₹28.5 crore and cash of only ₹2.8 crore at 30 September.
Margin dilution while new hospitals stay below 50% occupancy, against the 13-14% margin guidance.
Data privacy and cybersecurity exposure as patient data grows, with the app and AI engine still in pilot.
Goa resort economics unknown until it is repurposed; diagnostics and app monetisation are not yet defined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and expansion, but defensive on the occupancy decline, with several answers unclear or repeated. Figures on bed count, occupancy and revenue were inconsistent across answers, and several questions were deferred to next quarter.
